subject: Implementation kickoff & access patterns for Mediq private deployment
messages:
From: Sabrina Cole <sabrina.cole@mediq.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.hughes@mediq.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:01:00 -0800
Subject: Implementation kickoff & initial access questions

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks for the intro — excited to get this moving. We're starting our internal planning for the private deployment and have a few early questions so we can align network and security teams before the kickoff workshop: 

- Do you have a preferred CIDR size for VPC peering (we currently use multiple /24s for prod vs. stage)?
- For private endpoints, will Redwood support regional DNS names (we need to map against our split-horizon DNS)?
- On the on-prem package: is there an offline installer or does Redwood require live outbound access for agent telemetry?

I've attached a simple worksheet with our current subnets and a tentative firewall rule list (Attachment: mediq-network-workbook.xlsx). Please confirm the right people on your side; I'll loop in our infra team after we have your ask list.

Thanks,
Sabrina Cole
VP, Cloud Engineering
Mediq Health
(Attachment: mediq-network-workbook.xlsx)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Cole <sabrina.cole@mediq.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff & initial access questions

Hi Sabrina — great to meet you.

Quick answers up front and a short plan: 

- CIDR: We typically recommend a /22 for customer VPCs when multiple subnets (prod/stage/bastion) will be peered; that avoids collisions with common /24s. If you need tighter ranges we can handle /24s but will surface any overlap during the network review.
- DNS: Redwood supports split-horizon DNS for private endpoints; we'll provide the private FQDNs for the endpoint IPs. We can also publish a DNS record set you can import into your Route53 / Azure DNS.
- On-prem package: There is an offline on-prem bundle (signed tar) for air-gapped installs. For our standard private deployment we do recommend outbound TLS to our control-plane endpoints for metrics and alerts, but that can be routed through customer-managed proxies. The offline bundle is only for fully air-gapped customers.

Plan / owners: 
- Evelyn (me): primary CS lead and SRE/architecture liaison
- Ben Carter: networking and Dedicated ops (will run the peering runbook)
- Hannah Schmitt: implementation PM and schedule owner

Next steps: can we schedule the 60-min technical deep-dive next week? I'll bring the draft runbook and a short checklist (Attachment: redwood-private-onprem-checklist.pdf).

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-private-onprem-checklist.pdf)

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff & initial access questions

Sabrina — adding a few operational details from the peering/runbook side: 

1) Peering approach: we prefer a peering connection per environment (prod/stage). If you want a single VPC with multiple subnets that's fine too. We'll exchange VPC IDs, account IDs, and the target CIDRs during the pre-flight.

2) Route tables & NAT: For the private endpoints we put them in a dedicated subnet with a managed route table. If you have NAT gateways for egress please confirm the SNAT ranges so we can whitelist in any external proxies.

3) Security groups / firewall: We'll provide a minimal port list — TCP:443, 10250 (if you choose the host-agent), and UDP 123 for NTP where applicable. For on-prem we prefer mTLS between services; if you have mTLS termination at a load balancer let us know the cert rotation workflow.

4) Audit / logs: we will push audit logs to a customer-owned S3 or syslog endpoint. If you need SOC 2 evidence during onboarding, note that in the kickoff so we can prepare the evidence pack.

I can walk through the peering steps during the call — propose Tue 2026-11-17 10:00 PT / Wed 11:00 CT (you pick).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sabrina — thanks for the worksheet. I pulled out the key fields we'll need for the network review and added a short onboarding timeline below. Please reply inline in the sheet if anything looks off.

Onboarding timeline (draft):
- Week 0: Pre-flight network review + confirm CIDRs and firewall list
- Week 1: Technical kickoff (60m) — runbook walkthrough, roles, and scheduling of peering maintenance window
- Week 2: Provision private endpoints and peering; internal smoke tests
- Week 3: On-prem bundle deployment (if applicable) + integration tests
- Week 4: Cutover and monitoring handoff; run through rollback plan

Request: could you confirm if your security team requires HSM-backed KMS for key storage? If so we'll include HSM integration and procedures in the runbook (it adds ~3 business days to the timeline for cert provisioning).

Also sharing our internal planning doc (paste link below) — it has a short checklist and the standard post-install validation steps.

- Mediq will allocate a /22 for the peering (we'll reserve 10.32.0.0/22 for Redwood).
